title: Activepieces on Kubernetes: How Self-Hosting Works in 2026
summary: Activepieces on Kubernetes involves specific infrastructure considerations and trade-offs. Determine whether self-hosting fits your automation needs.
body_markdown:
## What running it yourself costs and requires


Although the Community Edition is free under the MIT licence, the cluster, its idle capacity and an engineer's hours aren't.


### Licence and plan boundaries


Check the vendor's[pricing page](https://www.activepieces.com/pricing) rather than trusting a summary: as of 24 October 2026 it is the only authority on plans. **The MIT-licensed Community Edition costs nothing to run** , so any licence fee you budget is for a paid plan, not for the code.


> Although the Community Edition is free under the MIT licence, the cluster, its idle capacity and an engineer's hours aren't.


If your security review requires SSO beyond the Team plan, audit logs or embedding, the free edition won't pass it, and all three go through the[sales form](https://www.activepieces.com/sales) . SOC 2 is in progress, not certified, so don't enter it as held on a vendor questionnaire.


Buying those controls doesn't mean accepting a lesser build because you host it yourself. Activepieces runs SSO and SCIM, custom RBAC, audit logs, release management and secret manager integration identically on your own servers, fully air-gapped, and on its managed cloud.


Regulated and public-sector organisations already operate the air-gapped edition in production, and MoneyGram, Moneypenny, Alan and FundingSocieties run Activepieces as well. Those features live in` packages/ee/` under a separate commercial licence, outside the MIT-licensed core.


### Infrastructure and people costs


Before a single node exists, the managed control plane is already billed. The chart sets the monthly fee for each cloud's Kubernetes service beside the hosted plans.


Take from it that the cluster fee alone can exceed a whole hosted subscription: $73 on EKS is more than three times the $20 Plus plan and about a third of the $200 Team plan, which means infrastructure alone costs more than an entire service tier.


Most of what you provision sits idle, and nodes are the larger line.[Cast AI](https://cast.ai/press-release/cast-ai-analysis-finds-only-13-percent-of-provisioned-cpus-and-20-percent-of-memory-is-utilized/) found that **provisioned CPU is mostly unused** : 11% used on AWS, 11% on Azure and 17% on GCP, which means you're paying to maintain capacity that sits mostly idle.


Even on the best of those, over four-fifths of the cores you pay for do nothing.


Somebody has to patch the cluster, rotate certificates and answer the page at 3am. Neither the pricing page nor the chart carries that cost, and you must price it yourself.


### Where the hosted cloud is the better choice


If nobody on the team already operates a cluster, **the control-plane fee is only part of the cost** of what you'd be buying.


The hosted cloud at $20 or $200 a month replaces the cluster, the upgrades and the on-call rota, sparing your team from these three operational burdens, so they redirect those hours to building features instead.


Start on the hosted plan to test your flows, and return to the cluster question only when a requirement such as data residency or an audit log forces it. Builders can[start free](https://cloud.activepieces.com/sign-up?ap_cta=blog_body&ref=%2Fblog%2Factivepieces-on-kubernetes-how-self-hosting-works-in-2026) ; teams that need self-hosted enterprise features should use the sales form.
